gallery.title: File:William W. Averell.jpg
gallery.credit: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, Brady's National Photographic Portrait Galleries  The exact same photo was published near the front of History of the Third Pennsylvania Cavalry, Sixtieth Regiment Pennsylvania Volunteers, in the American Civil War, 1861-1865., Volume 3, Part 4, which was published by the Franklin Printing Company in Philadelphia in 1905. The author is listed as United States, 3rd Pennsylvania Calvary Regiment. The cover of the book says William Brooke Rawie, and the inside says "Compiled by the Regimental History Committee in Accordance with a Resolution of the Third Pennsylvania Cavalry Association." The OCLC number is 1683643.
gallery.description: William Woods Averell (1832–1900) was a United States Army officer and a cavalry general in the American Civil War. After the war he was a diplomat and became wealthy by inventing American asphalt pavement.

gallery.filename: Battle of White Sulphur Springs Plan.png
gallery.title: File:Battle of White Sulphur Springs Plan.png
gallery.credit: This is a crop of an 1864 map created by Alvin Jewett Johnson.  The entire map can be found in the Library of Congress here, and shows Virginia, Delaware, Maryland & West Virginia. Text box and arrows etc. were added by TwoScarsUp based on description in the book The Battle of White Sulphur Springs by Eric J. Wittenberg.
gallery.source: Battle of White Sulphur Springs Plan
gallery.description: A Union Army brigade commanded by Brigadier General William W. Averell planned a raid with multiple objectives. It was unable to accomplish its third objective because it was stopped by a Confederate force command by George S. Patton in the Battle of White Sulphur Springs.

gallery.filename: Battle of White Sulphur Springs Union Map.png
gallery.title: File:Battle of White Sulphur Springs Union Map.png
gallery.artist: Published under the direction of the U.S. Secretaries of War by Major George B. Davis (U.S. Army), Leslie J. Perry (civilian expert), and Joseph W. Kirkley (civilian expert). The map itself was drawn by Lieutenant John R. Meigs, who was present at the battle. The map has been enhanced and identifiers added by TwoScarsUp.
gallery.credit: This a crop of a map of the Battle of White Sulphur Springs, which occurred on August 26-27, 1863, in the American Civil War.  The drawing is by a Union officer.  A Confederate force led by Colonel George S. Patton defeated Br. General William W. Averell. The map can be found in the Library of Congress here.
gallery.source: Battle of White Sulphur Springs Union Map
gallery.description: The map is from Plate CXXXV-B, No. 3, from the Atlas to Accompany the Official Records of the Union and Confederate Armies. It shows the Battle of White Sulphur Springs, which occurred on August 26-27, 1863, in the American Civil War. The Union brigade commanded by Br. Gen. William W. Averell was stopped by a Confederate force commanded by Col. George Patton.
